s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic inflammation with polyarthritis and granulomatous lesions
salient_findings: Six weeks of low-grade fever and fatigue
Multiple dull red tender nodules on the forehead, cheek, and sternum
Bilateral upper and mid-zone parenchymal infiltrates with nodular lesions on chest radiograph
key_facts: No history of high-risk sexual behavior
Negative for antinuclear antibodies, IgM-rheumatoid factor, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, antistreptolysin O, and anti-DNase B antibodies
Normal serum calcium and angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative urine examination for Gonococci spp.
Negative serum Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test for syphilis
Skin lesion biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation with suppuration
Cervical lymph node biopsy: Large areas of necrosis rimmed by epithelioid cell granulomas with occasional Langhans' multinucleated giant cells
Ziehl-Neelsen staining: Positive for acid-fast bacilli

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli and granulomatous inflammation with suppuration in skin and lymph node biopsies

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and polyarthritis, although lack of small joint involvement and negative serum calcium and angiotensin-converting enzyme levels are atypical

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous lesions and polyarthritis, but absence of upper respiratory symptoms and negative antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies are unusual

shortlist.label: Chronic granulomatous disease
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring granulomatous lesions and inflammation, but patient's age and lack of recurrent infections are atypical

shortlist.label: Blau syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous dermatitis, arthritis, and recurrent granulomatous lesions, although rare and typically presents in childhood

raw.rationale: The presence of acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, granulomatous inflammation with suppuration in skin lesion biopsy, and epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans' multinucleated giant cells in cervical lymph node biopsy are characteristic findings of tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Normal serum calcium and angiotensin-converting enzyme levels, and lack of other typical findings such as small joint involvement or diurnal variation of symptoms

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Negative antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies and lack of typical respiratory or renal symptoms

rejected.label: Chronic granulomatous disease
rejected.why: Age of onset and lack of recurrent infections typical of chronic granulomatous disease

rejected.label: Blau syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of family history and typical dermatologic or ocular findings
